findings.message: The diff changes plugin code (hooks/core/gate.ts, README, tests) under plugins/specclaw-mod/ but bumps no version. Bump specclaw-mod, and every other plugin, to the same version in each plugins/*/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, each plugins/*/.codex-plugin/plugin.json and every plugins[] entry in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json.
findings.scenario: A user installed the previous specclaw-mod version. This gate behaviour change (case-insensitive matching, narrower state.json carve-out) ships under the same version number, so installed copies are never updated.

findings.message: The glob `./tests/*.spec.ts` excludes register.test.ts. That file imports 'claude-code/testing' and runs only under `claude plugin test`. When `claude` is not on PATH the script sets RESULT=PARTIAL but still exits 0. A runner that has skipped the only test for the double-dispatch fix therefore reports success. Exit non-zero (or a distinct code) when the claude-based steps did not run, or fail in CI.
findings.scenario: A CI runner without `claude` runs run-mod-tests.sh. The bun specs pass, the register test never runs, and the script exits 0. Reverting the register.tsx fix keeps CI green.

findings.message: The test covers one failure mode only: the `session.cwd` handler throws. The previous round asked for both a rejecting refresh and a synchronously throwing refresh, because `.catch` does not intercept a synchronous throw. Add rows for both shapes. Assert the returned tool result (`{ result: { stdout: 'ok' } }`), not just `deny === undefined`. The two commands in the loop exercise the same path and add no variant. The test also never runs under `bun test`, so there is no evidence it fails without the fix.
findings.scenario: refresh throws synchronously before returning a promise, after the tool has run. The `.catch` never fires and the error escapes the handler. The test still passes because it only exercises one throw shape and never inspects the result.

findings.message: The path is lowercased on every platform. On case-sensitive filesystems (Linux), a sibling directory that differs only in case is a different directory but is now treated as inside the project. The previous finding asked for case-insensitivity on Windows and macOS. Either gate it on platform or document it as a deliberate fail-closed trade-off.
findings.scenario: Linux, cwd=/work/app, path=/work/App/x.ts (an unrelated directory). The gate now denies the edit when no change is approved, where before it returned ALLOW.

findings.message: The new `/i` flags on EXEMPT and STATE_FILE have no test rows. Add `/repo/.SpecClaw/changes/x/state.json` (deny), `/repo/.specclaw/changes/x/STATE.JSON` (deny) and `/repo/.GIT/config` (allow). Also add a deny row for state.json nested deeper than `changes/<name>/`, since the carve-out is narrower than the old `endsWith('/state.json')`.
findings.scenario: Dropping the `i` flag from STATE_FILE leaves every row in AC6 green, even though `.SPECCLAW/changes/x/state.json` would then become editable.
